ranking.note: Raised to P1: settles the kernel logging API design that #33847, #30342 and #34775 all depend on, and removes logging.cpp from the kernel library; the decision is blocking three other PRs before API stabilization.
Lowered to P4: removal of two redundant C API accessors with no consumer asking is exactly the cosmetic API polish the category puts below P3.

inconsistencies: Logging cluster (#34374, #33847, #30342, #34775) must be read as one design decision, not four independent PRs. #34775 makes the kernel log callback explicitly global while #33847 attaches logging connections to contexts with per-connection levels; these pull in opposite directions. Review #34374 first (it defines the structured log entry and drops logging.cpp from the kernel), then decide global-vs-per-context, then #33847, then #30342.

Fatal/runtime error propagation is being attacked three times: #29700 (return util::Result/FlushResult from validation and blockstorage), #35646 (remove M_ERROR from ValidationState via util::Expected), #36326 (typed kernel::FatalError/FlushError for notifications). They overlap substantially at the same boundary; #29700 is the broadest and should be reviewed/decided first, with #35646 treated as an RFC on the same ground to avoid duplicated rework.

#35646 and #36318 both change ValidationState error semantics (#35646 removes the runtime-error state, #36318 adds BLOCK_INCONCLUSIVE and an Assume invariant that every invalid state has a result). Whichever lands first forces a rebase of the other; sequence them deliberately.
#33117 is mostly interfaces::Node / GUI plumbing for assumeutxo rather than the kernel C API; it sits in this category only weakly, and its real beneficiaries are the GUI PRs it unblocks.

#35662 and #32427 change validation / block storage substantively as well as the kernel boundary (PrecomputedTransactionData lifetime; replacing BlockTreeDB with a WAL store). Both are kernel and validation; the validation half should be reviewed with validation eyes, and #32427 in particular may warrant splitting.
result.notes: No PR here carries a fund-safety, security or supported-platform failure, so the band spread is driven by the category's own criteria: boundary correctness and decoupling first, new embedder capabilities next, optional developer APIs and cosmetic surface trimming last. Two chains dominate the list (logging, fatal-error propagation); reviewing the head of each chain buys more than any individual leaf PR.
